sections.title: Older Houses, Longer Repair Lists
body: Princeton's homes skew old even by Mercer County standards. The Census Bureau's American Community Survey counts about 30,756 residents here and puts the median year built at 1965. Nearly a quarter of the housing (23%) dates to 1939 or earlier, against 18% for the county, and 64% was built before 1980. Just over half of homes (54%) are single-family detached, 55% of occupied homes are lived in by their owners, and the median home has 6.3 rooms, more than the county's 5.7.

None of that tells you what is wrong with one particular house, but homes of that age tend to share some habits. Frames drift as a building settles, so a door that latched for decades starts to rub. Walls may be plaster on lath rather than drywall, and cracked plaster wants a plaster repair, not a drywall patch screwed over it. Old trim profiles are not always on the shelf, so a replacement piece may have to be matched as closely as the stock allows. As a local handyman in Princeton, we settle the price for that kind of fitting work before we start, not halfway through.

The other end of the range matters too: 19% of Princeton homes were built in 2000 or later. Those lists look different, usually builder-grade faucets wearing out, caulk joints opening up, and deck boards that have weathered.

sections.title: One Princeton Since 2013
body: Princeton as a single municipality is young. The borough split from Princeton Township in 1894 in a dispute over school taxes, and the two governed separately until voters in both approved a merger in November 2011. The combined municipality took effect on January 1, 2013. Earlier merger attempts kept failing over zoning, because the old borough was densely built while the township around it had more widely spaced properties.

Today the town covers 18.41 square miles just south of Princeton Ridge and borders seven municipalities: Hopewell Township, Lawrence Township, and West Windsor in Mercer County, Plainsboro and South Brunswick in Middlesex, and Franklin and Montgomery in Somerset. Older place names such as Cedar Grove, Port Mercer, Princeton Basin, and Jugtown still carry their own identities inside it.

That old split between a compact center and a spread-out township can still shape a repair list. A house on a tighter lot often has a list that stays indoors: a loose stair rail, an interior door, a plaster crack, a fixture. A house on a larger parcel tends to add a gate, a run of fence, or a few deck boards. The flat packages are the same in 08540 and 08542 either way.

sections.title: What Princeton Owners Ask Us to Fix
body: Most visits bundle several small items into one trip. These are the categories we take on, each with its own page explaining what fits a Visit, a Half Day, or a Full Day:
items: [Drywall and plaster repair](/drywall-repair): cracks, holes, and stained ceilings, with plaster repaired as plaster
[Doors and locks](/doors): sticking doors planed and rehung, slabs fitted to existing frames, deadbolts
[Carpentry and trim](/carpentry): loose banisters, damaged casing and baseboard, built-in shelving
[Fixture and faucet swaps](/fixture-swaps): faucets, toilets, light fixtures, and switches replaced like-for-like
[Tile, grout, and caulk](/tile-grout-caulk): tubs recaulked, showers regrouted, cracked tiles swapped
[Painting touch-ups](/painting-touch-ups): a repaired wall or one room brought back to a single color
[Deck and fence repair](/deck-fence-repair): boards, rails, posts, and gates
[Grab bars](/grab-bar-installation) anchored into framing, not drywall

sections.title: Ordinary Maintenance Under the State Code
body: New Jersey's Uniform Construction Code sets aside a category called ordinary maintenance, defined at N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, that needs no construction permit in a one- or two-family home. It includes interior and exterior painting, drywall or plaster work covering less than 25% of a wall area, trim and moldings, a door replaced in the same opening without changing the framing, attached furnishings such as cabinets and bathroom accessories, like-material repairs to non-structural deck, porch, and stoop parts, and swapping a faucet, light fixture, switch, or receptacle for a similar one.

Our work is built around that list. Anything that changes structure, moves a pipe, or adds a circuit needs a permit from Princeton's municipal construction office, and that belongs to a contractor or licensed trade who will pull it. If something you send us crosses that line, you hear it from us before you buy parts.

sections.title: Paint in a Pre-1978 Princeton Home
body: With 64% of Princeton's housing built before 1980, a large share of homes here predate 1978, the cutoff the federal lead paint rules use. Under the EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule (40 CFR 745), work in pre-1978 housing that disturbs more than 6 square feet of painted surface per room indoors, or more than 20 square feet outside, has to follow lead-safe work practices and be done by an EPA-certified firm.

Many small repairs stay well under those amounts: a hinge, a strike plate, a faucet, one cracked tile. Sanding down a whole door, opening a section of old wall, or scraping exterior trim can go over. Send photos and the year the house was built, and before anything is scheduled we will tell you which side of the threshold the job lands on and whether it calls for a certified firm.

sections.title: Flat Packages, National Numbers, Written Terms
body: We price by package. A Visit is $345 for up to 2 hours, a Half Day is $595 for up to 4 hours, and a Full Day is $1,095 for up to 8 hours. An itemized job is billed at $175 an hour but never above the package it fits in, and materials are quoted up front on the same estimate.

For comparison, HomeGuide's national handyman cost guide (August 2023) lists $50-$80 an hour for self-employed handymen and $75-$125 an hour for company handymen, plus materials, with minimum charges commonly $75-$200 and a $30-$80 trip charge when someone has to go buy supplies. Its drywall guide puts patching a hole under 4 inches at $300-$500. Those are national averages, not Princeton quotes, but they are a fair yardstick when you compare home repair services.

Any home improvement job over $500 gets a written, signed contract, as New Jersey's Contractors' Registration Act and the state's home improvement regulations require: start and completion dates, the total price, and our registration number, NJ HIC #13VH13918800. You then have three business days to cancel.

faqs.question: Do you repair plaster walls in older Princeton houses?
faqs.answer: Yes. Plaster gets repaired as plaster rather than covered with a drywall patch. In a house built before 1978 we look at how much painted surface the repair will disturb first, since a larger opening can cross the EPA lead rule thresholds described above. See [drywall and plaster repair](/drywall-repair) for what a typical job includes.

faqs.question: Can one trip cover several small items?
faqs.answer: That is how most Princeton jobs go. Send the whole list with photos. If it fits in two hours it is the $345 [Visit](/handyman); if not, we quote a Half Day or Full Day before you book.

sections.title: A Housing Stock Split Down the Middle
body: Lawrence sits right on the line between older and newer housing. According to the Census Bureau's American Community Survey, the township's median year built is 1979, and 51% of its homes went up before 1980. Only 8% date to 1939 or earlier, well below the Mercer County share of 18%, and 14% were built in 2000 or later. Two thirds of occupied homes (67%) are owner-occupied, just under half (49%) are single-family detached, and the median home has 5.8 rooms.

A house built around 1979 is now more than forty years old, the age when many original parts are due. That is a general pattern, not a promise about any one house, but it often means interior doors that no longer close cleanly, bathroom grout and caulk that have given up, exterior wood trim softening near the ground, and light fixtures or faucets that have simply worn out. Hiring a Lawrence Township handyman for that list makes more sense than calling separate trades for each item.

sections.title: We Don't Do Remodels. Here Is What We Do Instead.
body: People find this page while searching for remodeling and additions in Lawrence Township, so to be plain: we do not build additions, finish basements, or remodel kitchens and bathrooms. Those are general contractor projects that need permits, plans, and inspections, and they are not our business.

What we do is the repair and refresh work that often makes a remodel unnecessary. A tired bathroom can come back with fresh grout, new silicone, and two replaced tiles through [tile, grout, and caulk repair](/tile-grout-caulk), plus a new faucet or toilet through [fixture swaps](/fixture-swaps). A kitchen can look different after a [backsplash](/backsplash) goes up. Dated rooms often need [painting touch-ups](/painting-touch-ups) and new interior [doors](/doors) more than they need new walls. If your project really is a remodel, we will tell you so and you can take it to a general contractor.

sections.title: From Maidenhead to Lawrenceville
body: The township began as Maidenhead Township in 1697, named by Quaker settlers after a village on the Thames, and was renamed Lawrence Township in 1816 for Captain James Lawrence, the War of 1812 naval commander remembered for the order Don't give up the ship. It covers 21.98 square miles and borders Ewing, Hamilton, Hopewell Township, Princeton, Trenton, and West Windsor.

Many residents call the whole township Lawrenceville, since most use a Lawrenceville mailing address, while others have Princeton or Trenton addresses. If your house is in Lawrence Township, the same pricing applies whatever your envelope says. Place names such as Eldridge Park, Slackwood, Colonial Lakelands, Franklin Corner, and Port Mercer all sit partly or fully inside the township.

Weather has left a mark here too. On September 23, 2003, an F1 tornado followed a path along Princeton Pike and damaged homes. Damage of that scale is insurance and contractor territory, but the smaller aftermath of a rough season, a fence section down or a gate that no longer latches, is [deck and fence repair](/deck-fence-repair) work.

sections.title: Repairs Lawrence Homeowners Book Most
body: A single trip usually handles a mix. Here is how a Lawrence list tends to break down by service:
items: Drafty or binding entry and interior [doors](/doors), new weatherstripping and sweeps
Wall cracks, ceiling stains, and holes from old anchors patched through [drywall repair](/drywall-repair)
Exterior trim and rotted wood rebuilt, banisters firmed up, via [carpentry](/carpentry)
Dryer vents cleared, screens fixed, detectors replaced in a [home maintenance](/home-maintenance) visit
TVs, mirrors, shelves, and flat-pack furniture handled under [TV mounting and assembly](/tv-mounting)
Faucets and light fixtures swapped like-for-like through [fixture swaps](/fixture-swaps)

sections.title: No Permit for Like-for-Like Work
body: The state construction code, at N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, lists ordinary maintenance that one- and two-family homes can have done without a permit. Painting, trim, new flooring material, drywall or plaster repair under 25% of a wall area, replacing a door in its existing opening, cabinets and bathroom accessories, like-for-like repairs to non-structural deck and porch parts, and replacing a faucet, toilet, switch, receptacle, or light fixture with a similar one all fall in that category.

Everything we do in Lawrence stays inside it. New circuits, relocated plumbing, structural changes, and additions go through the township's construction office for permits, and those are jobs for licensed trades and general contractors.

sections.title: Lead Rules for the Older Half
body: Half the township's homes were built before 1980, and plenty of those predate 1978. In pre-1978 housing, the EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule (40 CFR 745) kicks in when work disturbs more than 6 square feet of painted surface in a room, or more than 20 square feet on the exterior. Past that point the work must follow lead-safe practices and be carried out by an EPA-certified firm.

Swapping a lockset or a faucet does not come near those numbers. Stripping a door, cutting out a large wall section, or scraping a porch might. Tell us the year your house was built when you send photos, and we will say before scheduling whether the job stays under the line.

sections.title: How Our Prices Compare
body: Three flat packages: Visit, $345, up to 2 hours; Half Day, $595, up to 4 hours; Full Day, $1,095, up to 8 hours. Single items are priced at $175 an hour, capped at the package they fall into. Materials appear on the quote before you agree to anything.

HomeGuide's national survey of handyman prices, published August 2023, gives hourly rates of $50 to $80 for independent handymen and $75 to $125 for corporate ones, materials extra. It also reports minimum charges usually between $75 and $200 and trip charges of $30 to $80 for supply runs. These are national numbers rather than Lawrence quotes.

Jobs over $500 come with a signed written contract showing start and completion dates, the full price, and our New Jersey registration number, as the Contractors' Registration Act and state home improvement rules require. After signing you have three business days to cancel.

faqs.question: Will you build an addition or finish my basement?
faqs.answer: No. Additions and basement finishing are permitted general contractor projects. We handle the repairs around the house instead: [doors](/doors), [drywall](/drywall-repair), [carpentry](/carpentry), and like-for-like [fixture swaps](/fixture-swaps).

faqs.question: My mailing address says Princeton or Trenton. Do you cover me?
faqs.answer: Yes. Part of Lawrence Township uses Princeton or Trenton mailing addresses. If the house is in the township, the flat packages on our [handyman page](/handyman) apply.
